title: Asymptotic Notations
summary: The six asymptotic notations of the course: O, Omega, Theta, o, omega and tilde. Includes intuitive interpretation, formal definition, criteria with limits in the two conventions and worked examples.

learningObjectives.text: Explain why asymptotic notations summarize the behavior of a function ignoring constants and terms of lower growth.
Correctly identify which function is f and which is g before applying a criterion with limits.
Define Big-O as an upper bound and apply your criteria with limits in the two conventions.
Define Omega as a lower bound and apply your criteria with limits in the two conventions.
Define Theta as an exact bound and recognize that its limit criterion is the same in both conventions.
Define little-o as a strict upper bound and differentiate it from Big-O.
Define little-omega as a strict lower bound and differentiate it from Omega.
Define the tilde or tilde as exact asymptotic equivalence and distinguish it from Theta.
Solve examples using both the lim f/g convention and the lim g/f course convention.

terms.label: Asymptotic notation
terms.definition: Way to summarize the growth behavior of a function when n tends to infinity, ignoring constants and lower order terms.

terms.label: f(n)
terms.definition: Function that is analyzed or whose membership in an asymptotic family is to be demonstrated.

terms.label: g(n)
terms.definition: Reference function against which f(n) is compared.

terms.label: Big-O
terms.definition: Upper bound. It indicates that f does not grow faster than g, except for a multiplicative constant.

terms.label: Big-Omega
terms.definition: Lower bound. It indicates that f does not grow slower than g, except for a multiplicative constant.

terms.label: Theta
terms.definition: Exact bound. It indicates that f and g grow at the same asymptotic rate.

terms.label: little-o
terms.definition: Strict upper bound. It indicates that f grows strictly slower than g.

terms.label: little-omega
terms.definition: Strict lower bound. It indicates that f grows strictly faster than g.

terms.label: Tilde
terms.definition: Exact asymptotic equivalence. It indicates that f and g are asymptotically identical and their quotient tends to 1.

terms.label: Convention B / course
terms.definition: Limits convention used in the course comparing g(n)/f(n).
